sampling_model.design: Independent multinomial sampling from the selected law \(p=P(E,W,Z\mid S=1)\), with an independent margin multinomial sample in design A when margins are estimated and \(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\).
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes one draw of \((E,W,Z)\) conditional on \(S=1\); the finite SCM is a superpopulation model.
sampling_model.treatment: \(X\) is binary and may be confounded with the response type; in design B its assignment probability may depend on \((U,Z)\).
sampling_model.overlap: All selected cells are positive. Supplied design-A margins remain observed inputs, but their positivity is forced whenever the full fiber is nonempty because \(P(E=e)\ge P(E=e,S=1)=c r_e>0\). Wald inference is restricted to first-order-compatible charts with \(\eta_{\chi}\ge\varepsilon\), twice continuously differentiable chart extensions, positive distance from incompatible chart closures, and \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Reduced multinomial coordinates use empirical frequencies and the explicit block-diagonal estimator \(\widehat\Omega_n\). The deterministic \(n^{-1/4}\) rule selects the first certified separated rigid chart; if none exists, the estimator uses its declared numerical fallback and the reported region is \([0,1]^2\). Transition inference uses a profile multinomial deviance, a \(1-\beta_n\) Clopper--Pearson preliminary region, and Berger--Boos exact nuisance calibration.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 identify PN and PS under positive observed tables, invertible proxy matrices, and unequal determinant-ratio conditions.
Formula (5) identifies a causal effect under a proxy rank condition without identifying the measurement mechanism.
Proposition 3.3 characterizes infinitesimal rigidity of an exact nonnegative factorization by its admissible-motion cone.
Theorems 5--9 give necessary support conditions and sufficient sequential recovery conditions for selected NMF factors.
Theorem 1 gives sufficient positive-scattering thresholds for minimality and uniqueness of nonnegative tensor decompositions.
Theorem 3.4 gives a regular root-n estimator for a linear proximal target without uniqueness of the bridge solution.

Theorem 1 identifies all four response-type probabilities in a randomized experiment under positive conditional tables, \(W\perp Z\mid U\), \(X\perp(U,Z,W)\), invertible cell matrices, and unequal determinant ratios; equations (8)--(11) give plug-in estimators.

Theorem 1 identifies all four joint probabilities of binary potential-outcome types under Figure 2(b)'s IV-plus-proxy recursive factorization, the five invertibility requirements in condition (i), the cross-treatment second-column separation in condition (ii), and the two exclusion restrictions in condition (iii).

Theorems 2--5 give sound closed-form bounds for a representative family of discrete probabilities of causation from standard experimental and observational distributions, while general-dimensional tightness remains open in the current version.
Conditional quasi-likelihood-ratio tests have uniformly correct asymptotic size without strong identification.
E-variable inversion yields exact anytime-valid confidence sets for contingency-table parameters.
Theorem 4 identifies PN and PS under exogeneity and monotonicity, and equations (15)--(18) give sharp bounds otherwise.

body.tldr: For every labeled finite four-response-type model with outcome-dependent selection and proxy-cycle restrictions, the field-level kernel is a boundary-complete response-cycle atlas for PN/PS target rigidity. A structural compiler stratifies the full nonnegative fiber by observable ranks, supports, endpoint incidences, and cycle products; it treats supplied-margin two-proxy data and unknown-margin relevant-IV data through response-level shared-\(Z\) residual forests. The main theorem gives necessary and sufficient target-constancy conditions, exact coefficient-field values on rigid strata, and legal same-observable SCM twins on nonrigid strata. Supporting results verify agreement with published regular proxy formulas on their stated domains, including Kawakami's no-selection IV-plus-proxy theorem, and exhibit an explicit selected boundary law whose proxy-loading matrix violates Kawakami's invertibility condition while the atlas remains decisive. Positivity of compatible population margins follows from positive selected cells and \(c=P(S=1)>0\). Integer-polynomial certificates, isolating intervals, and bit bounds are reserved for explicitly rational tables. A total chart procedure uses a conservative full-square fallback when no separated rigid chart is certified; Wald inference is asserted only on certified separated charts, while calibrated confidence-fiber inversion remains honest at identification transitions.

project_justification.gap: Published no-selection and selected-proxy formulas identify response-type targets under regular matrix invertibility and separation, including Kawakami's IV-plus-proxy conditions, but they do not decide PN/PS constancy when ranks fall, assignment coefficients reach nonnegative faces, endpoints coincide, selection changes population margins, or shared-instrument equations couple unknown margins. General discrete-PoC compatible-model bounds do not impose the selected proxy factorizations or label their cycle components.
project_justification.niche: The four response types form a labeled cycle on which a two-dimensional causal target can be rigid even when the full factorization moves. Its selected proxy-cycle fiber is generally nonpolyhedral and differs from both Kawakami's regular no-selection IV-plus-proxy system and the compatible-model polytope used for unrestricted PoC bounds. The field-level problem is a global target-image classification across ranks, supports, real components, and induced-margin equations.
project_justification.fill: The response-cycle atlas gives necessary and sufficient target-constancy conditions over the selected four-type SCM class, returns coefficient-field targets or legal countermodels on every component and face, and handles both supplied-margin two-proxy and unknown-margin relevant-IV designs. Supporting overlap checks recover the published regular formulas; a separate explicit-law certificate records scope beyond Kawakami's invertibility domain without asserting subsumption or extension. Deterministic separated-chart Wald inference and exactly calibrated confidence-fiber inversion complete the statistical layer.

body.related_work: Shingaki, Yoshida, and Kuroki (2026), Theorem 1, Corollary 1, and Appendix equations (A.23)--(A.33), provide the selected four-response-type causal model and regular inversion formulas. The supporting anchor-agreement theorem verifies that the atlas returns the same PN/PS values under those conditions and records singular and boundary observable laws on which the atlas instead uses support-face or residual-forest certificates. Shingaki and Kuroki (2023), Theorem 1 and equations (8)--(11), identify and estimate all four response-type probabilities in a no-selection randomized experiment under \(W\perp Z\mid U\), treatment exogeneity, invertible cell matrices, and determinant-ratio separation. The experimental overlap theorem proves agreement after the label conversion \((00,01,10,11)=(4,2,3,1)\); the explicit selected assignment-boundary datum is a separate coverage check outside those experimental conditions. Kawakami (2021), Figure 2(b), equation (2), Theorem 1(i)--(iii) on page 12134, and the proof on pages 12135--12137 give the closer no-selection IV-plus-proxy comparison: the theorem assumes the recursive factorization, invertibility of \(A_{11,x}\), \(A_{22,x}\), \(A_x\), \(Q_{1,x}\), and \(P_{1,x}-Q_{1,x}\), cross-treatment separation of the second columns of the two displayed block ratios, and the exclusions \(Y_{x,z,w}=Y_x\) and \(X_{z,w}=X_z\); it identifies all four joint potential-outcome-type probabilities, with treatment-conditional weights recovered in the appendix for PN and PS. The supporting scope theorem records target agreement on the overlap and exhibits one selected boundary datum for which \(A_x\) is singular but the response-cycle atlas is rigid. This is an overlap and scope-separation comparison only; neither result is asserted to subsume or extend the other. Shu, Wang, and Li (2025, arXiv:2505.15274), Theorems 2--7, develop representative discrete PoC queries, equivalence and replaceability, and sound closed-form bounds from standard experimental and observational distributions; the current version reports low-dimensional computational tightness and leaves general-dimensional tightness open. That compatible-model characterization omits selected proxy-factorization restrictions and does not supply a labeled response-cycle target-constancy atlas. Its feasible region is a response-function polytope cut out by standard margins, whereas the present selected proxy-cycle fiber is generally nonpolyhedral and is cut out by proxy factorizations, supplied or induced margins, and selection restrictions; no inclusion relation is asserted. Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2018), formula (5), establishes that a causal functional can be identified without identifying its proxy mechanism, but treats an average effect under a linear proxy operator. Krone and Kubjas (2021), Proposition 3.3, supplies admissible-motion cones and separates infinitesimal, local, and global NMF rigidity. Gillis and Rajk\'o (2023), Theorems 5--9, provides partial factor-identifiability and sequential recovery tools, while PN/PS can be rigid without recovery of the relevant columns. Wang and Yuan (2026), Theorem 1 and its matrix specialization, gives sufficient support-scattering uniqueness conditions rather than an if-and-only-if causal target criterion. Zhang et al. (2023), Theorem 3.4, informs regular inference under nuisance nonuniqueness. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016) informs weak-identification calibration, and Turner and Grünwald (2022) supplies exact contingency-table inversion; here a Berger--Boos calibrated profile deviance is inverted through the changing legal SCM correspondence. Tian and Pearl (2000) supplies the published PN/PS benchmark used only as a validation corollary on the no-selection, treatment-exogenous, monotone submodel.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The all-rank-two two-proxy branch and the residual-ratio reduction have strong presolve support, but the complete mixed-support gluing theorem is unproved. Generic fixed-dimensional real-algebraic decision procedures establish decidability only; reporting a two-copy quantifier-elimination test would not satisfy the proposed structural-classification contribution. For arbitrary real observables, exactness is relative to the ordered coefficient field and carries no bit-complexity claim. Integer-polynomial certificates, rational isolating intervals, and bit bounds apply only to explicitly rational inputs. The Kawakami comparison is limited to agreement on its no-selection regular conditions and one explicit selected boundary law violating its Theorem 1(i) invertibility condition; no subsumption or extension is claimed. No claim is made that every rigid target is rational, that every boundary ambiguity has strictly positive twins, or that confidence sets shrink at genuinely unidentified collision laws.
body.honest_scope: The central open content is Open-ended Question 1, and the proposal is field-tier. The proposed theorem permits coefficient-field algebraic outputs and requires strict-positive twins only for interior nonrigid strata. Integer-polynomial certificates and bit bounds require explicitly encoded rational observables. Population-margin positivity is not maintained independently: every compatible law with positive selected cells and \(c=P(S=1)>0\) satisfies it, while design-A margins remain supplied observables. The chart evaluator, estimator, covariance output, and reported region are total; absence of a certified separated rigid chart triggers the declared numerical and full-square fallbacks. Covariance consistency and Wald coverage are asserted only for first-order-compatible charts separated from incompatible chart closures, with twice continuously differentiable extensions, proportional margin sampling when needed, and target covariance bounded away from singularity. Confidence-fiber inversion provides honest coverage at every transition; first-order Hausdorff agreement with Wald is asserted only on separated regular strata, and no shrinking-diameter assertion is made at genuinely unidentified laws. The Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki and Shingaki--Kuroki statements are supporting overlap-agreement and boundary-coverage checks, not comparative extension claims. Kawakami's no-selection IV-plus-proxy result is compared through its Figure 2(b), equation (2), and Theorem 1(i)--(iii): agreement is claimed only on the common regular scope, and the explicit selected boundary datum supplies only a strict scope separation through failure of \(A_x\) invertibility. Neither theorem is claimed to subsume or extend the other. The Shu--Wang--Li compatible-model polytope and the selected proxy-cycle fiber encode different information, so no subsumption claim is made. Known-selection reweighting is an implementation normalization. The Tian--Pearl validation applies to a specified \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) satisfying locally \(S=1\) almost surely, \(X\perp U\), and \(P_{\vartheta}(U=3)=0\); it proves the classical formulas for \(\tau(\vartheta)\), and identifies them with the unique element of \(\mathcal T_A(p,m)\) only when singleton rigidity is separately assumed. These local restrictions neither prove rigidity nor constrain either main design. The GEUVADIS analysis certifies consequences conditional on the stated proxy, exclusion, selection, and IV assumptions; population labels and genotype variables do not empirically prove those assumptions.
